paragraphs: A geared hand winch multiplies a person into several hundred kilograms of pull. The handle detaches because a winch that can be turned by anyone walking past is a winch that will eventually let go with somebody underneath it.
The model is light at 20,950 polygons and 20,835 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the handle detached. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $39 it suits industrial and equipment visualisation, tool marketing, e-commerce imagery, workshop and marine scenes, training material and game environments. On sale since 2025.

Slatted outdoor furniture solves rain by admitting defeat: water falls straight through, nothing pools, and the piece dries in minutes. The stripes are a consequence of that spacing rather than a decorative choice.
The set holds 42,888 polygons and 45,442 vertices, built in quads only with overlapping UVs, in green. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $39 it suits exterior and landscape visualisation, furniture marketing, e-commerce and catalogue imagery, terrace and cafe scenes, film sets and game environments. On sale since 2026.

A canister launched drone is stored, carried and fired from the same tube, which means the operator never assembles anything. That matters more than any performance figure: equipment that needs setting up is equipment that arrives late.
The model is light at 24,675 polygons and 25,439 vertices in quads and tris with mixed UV layout, in green, and carries StemCell certification.
At $39 it suits defence visualisation, news and documentary graphics, simulation, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2026.

The blowback pistol with a heavy slide is the cheapest way to make a handgun work, and this is the design that made that a category. It is inelegant, front heavy, and has sold in enormous numbers for exactly one reason.
The model holds 114,866 polygons and 57,790 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and carries StemCell certification.
At $39 it suits game weapons, film and television props, documentary and news graphics, simulation and editorial illustration. On sale since 2024.

The transfer board is the flexible circuit that carries every keystroke from the keyboard to the mainboard, and it is the part that fails when a laptop stops responding for no visible reason. Almost nobody has seen one.
The model holds 41,838 polygons and 42,297 vertices in quads and tris with overlapping UVs, and carries StemCell certification.
At $39 it suits technical documentation and repair visualisation, hardware marketing, exploded view illustration, education material and editorial work. On sale since 2026.

An M.2 drive is a stick of memory that replaced an entire mechanical device. There are no moving parts, no cable and no bay, and the whole thing is held down by a single screw, which is why storage stopped being a shape a laptop had to be designed around.
The model is extremely light at 2,217 polygons and 2,492 vertices, built in quads only with overlapping UVs. It carries StemCell certification.
At $39 it suits hardware and component visualisation, technical documentation, e-commerce imagery, exploded views, education material and editorial illustration. On sale since 2026.

Icebergs are freshwater, which surprises people: they calve from glaciers rather than freezing out of the sea. That is also why they are so blue in places, because the ice has been compressed for centuries with the air squeezed out of it.
The model holds 42,415 polygons and the same count of vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $39 it suits polar and marine visualisation, climate and documentary graphics, education material, film backgrounds, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2024.

Netting turns a pallet from a platform into a container. Everything above the deck is held by tension rather than by walls, which is lighter, faster to load and the only practical way to secure an irregular stack for air freight.
The model holds 219,087 polygons and 215,565 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in beige and black. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $39 it suits logistics and air freight visualisation, warehouse and apron scenes, equipment marketing, training material, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2025.

An open lid changes what a skip communicates. Closed it is infrastructure; open it is a scene, because whatever is inside becomes visible and the container starts telling the viewer something about the building it stands beside.
The model is light at 47,264 polygons and 24,054 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the lid open. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $39 it suits urban and industrial visualisation, waste management presentation, street and alley scenes, film backgrounds, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2024.

A weighbridge is a scale a lorry drives onto, and everything expensive about it is underneath. The deck has to flex almost not at all under forty tonnes, because the load cells are measuring a difference that a bending platform would hide.
The model holds 123,056 polygons and 136,692 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in steel blue. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $39 it suits logistics and industrial site visualisation, equipment marketing, quarry and depot scenes, training material, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2025.

The life vest is demonstrated on every flight and used on almost none. Inflated, it is a specific and slightly unsettling object, because the only circumstances in which anybody sees one that way are the ones nobody wants to picture.

The model holds 40,520 polygons and 80,378 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 6 maps all at 4096x4096, in the inflated state. It carries StemCell certification, and further vest builds are offered separately.
At $39 it suits aviation safety and training visualisation, cabin scenes, equipment marketing, film props, game assets and editorial illustration. On sale since 2020.

The monumental park entrance is a piece of set design doing narrative work. Timber and stone at a scale nobody needs, torches either side, and doors that open slowly: everything about it says that what is behind is both a destination and a warning.
The model holds 101,392 polygons and 52,129 vertices in quads and tris with overlapping UVs, and carries StemCell certification.
At $39 it suits film and television set visualisation, game environments, theme park and attraction presentation, concept art and editorial illustration. On sale since 2024.

The steering wheel became a control panel and nobody voted on it. Everything a driver adjusts without looking now lives on the spokes, which means the wheel is designed around thumb reach rather than around grip.
The model is light at 16,256 polygons and 18,132 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $39 it suits automotive interior visualisation, configurators and parts imagery, technical illustration, cockpit scenes, game assets and editorial work. On sale since 2025.

The gavel is almost entirely symbolic outside American courtrooms, and the book beside it is doing the same job: neither object is what actually decides anything, and both appear in every image ever made about the law.

The model holds 30,514 polygons and 31,432 vertices, built in quads only with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 14 maps, 3 at 4096x4096 and 11 at 2048x2048. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $39 it suits legal and editorial illustration, corporate and institutional visualisation, stock and advertising imagery, film set dressing, game props and education material. On sale since 2016.
